item: ODR-260 — A `thread_shared` value made `using` a memory manager
lens: SPEED AND IMPLEMENTATION: instructions and bytes per operation in the header, the hot path and at the boundary; the shape a compiler builds simply and a package decides from what it sees ([BLD-16]); the §X.4 row of each shape.
summary: Shape B as Hardened_3 applied it is the best of the eight shapes priced: `thread_shared T using A` is allowed for every manager, every owner is counted in the away count from the making line, the instance word (where [ALC-1] keeps one) stands in the header's 8-byte queue place, and the making line is `E7015` only where the value would hold a link to an instance of a manager that not every thread may call. It costs a program that never writes the word nothing (0 instructions, 0 bytes); for the value that does, the count path is chosen from the type at each line ([TYP-46] makes a plain place a `using Global` place, so every place names its values' manager) and is one locked add with its limit test, fewer instructions than the `Global` home path's chunk read, thread compare and mark test but more cycles on the making thread, the trade the programmer makes per value by the word (the row's 25% either way); the mark is a constant folded into the header's first store; the block is a bump in an arena and nothing at its end. The queue place is free for such a value because the only writer of the queue place is the subtract that takes the away count below zero ([RC-4] point 2), which cannot happen when every owner is in that count; placing the word there is also what keeps a class object's fields at one offset (32) whatever manager made it, so a method is compiled once. What the value loses by never being queued is nothing it could use: the queue exists to let the maker read the home count it alone writes, and a value with no home count has nothing to merge; its end on the ending thread is what [ALC-5]'s exclusivity check needs. The `static`-instance limit on the hand-over to an unscoped thread is right: keeping a local arena alive "another way" is a run-time count on the arena (a word and an atomic per value, verdict 107's cost returned) for a property that is compile-time data, and the language already has two zero-cost spellings, a scope from any instance and a `static` instance. Four wording and completeness edits make the text say what it means and close the one implementer question it left open: how a runtime routine that sees only a header (`ember_rt_object_release`) gives a `using`-made block back — by a `TypeInfo` per pair of type and manager kind, emitted by the package that makes one, nothing at run time.

alternatives_weighed.name: A: refuse every manager (E2114 after thread_shared)
alternatives_weighed.what: `using` may not follow `thread_shared`; every shared value's block comes from `Global`'s per-thread chunks (the method-3 team's answer, Hardened_2's refusing half).
alternatives_weighed.speed: Nothing new for the language, but the programmer cannot choose: every shared value made in bulk pays `Global`'s chunk-pool pop (thread-local load, free-list pop, ~8-12 instructions) and its free (an atomic exchange onto the chunk's returned list when the last owner ends elsewhere, plus the maker's takeover) instead of an arena bump (~4 instructions) and no free; memory per value a size class instead of the exact size; the end of a pipeline value waits for the maker's check point (peak memory higher). Verdict 107's measurements for `owns` values (a million small values 191 ms and 28.2 MB in an arena, C 191 ms) show the size of the lost option.
alternatives_weighed.readability: `thread_shared` becomes the one owner word `using` cannot follow (verdict 19 lists `using` after every owner word); a programmer who wrote `using level` is told to remove it for a reason (the chunk record) that counting away from birth removes.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: One counting path for all shared values is already lost to [RC-4] point 4's hand-over state and the K10 marks, which every implementation must have; `[TYP-46]`'s list would carry an exception K34 cannot restate as a property.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Drops a feature C++ (`std::allocate_shared` over a `pmr` resource) and Rust (`Arc::new_in`) have, for a hazard (an end delayed to a check point under an instance that may reset) that marking the value at its making removes; docs/AUTOPILOT.md §3 forbids dropping a feature to get past a check.

alternatives_weighed.name: B: allow every manager, counted away from birth, word in the queue place, E7015 by the property (applied)
alternatives_weighed.what: `thread_shared T using A` is a type; every owner is in the away count from the making line; the instance word, where kept, sits in the header's queue place; the making line and a place of the type are `E7015` where the value would hold a link to an instance of a manager that not every thread may call (a `ThreadShared` type whose `deallocate` and `reallocate` read `this`).
alternatives_weighed.speed: A program without the word: 0 instructions, 0 bytes. Making: `a.allocate(Layout(32 + size, align))` (arena: a bump and a limit test), a null test, and the same four header stores a `Global` value's making writes, the mark a constant in one of them. +1: one relaxed `fetch_add` and the limit test on its result (2 instructions, ~20 cycles uncontended on x86) against the home path's chunk-header load, thread-local compare, mark load, two branches and a plain add (~8 instructions, ~3-5 cycles when predicted). -1: one acquire-release subtract and a zero test; at zero the ended compare-exchange, `drop`, one atomic weak subtract, then `A.deallocate` as a direct call (nothing for an arena; a mask and a load for `FoundByAddress`; one load of the queue place else). Never the queue push, never a check point's work, the end never deferred. Header 32 bytes, 0 beyond it. Boundary: `ember_rt_object_release` tests the mark (one load and branch, paid for every value) and takes the away path. Rows: "A `thread_shared` value's two counts" and "A value made `using` a memory manager".
alternatives_weighed.safety: All when compiling: `E7015` where the end or growth would call a method that changes an instance from another thread (verdict 164's `sharedref mut` link as the model), `E3063` where the value would outlive its instance (an unscoped thread only from a `static`), `E3021` on a reset under it, `E7007` for two tasks growing in one instance; the mark set before any other thread can reach the block; the runtime's routines test the mark before any chunk read.
alternatives_weighed.readability: `using` means the same after every owner word; the refusal names the manager, the method and its line, and the lines to write.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: One code one rule (`E2114` keeps its meaning: no heap memory of its own; `E7015` the thread rule); every place's type names its manager, so the path is decided where the code is written ([BLD-16]).

alternatives_weighed.name: C: allow only for a manager whose type is `ThreadShared` (the flat marker test; Hardened_2's [TYP-46a], design 1)
alternatives_weighed.what: `thread_shared T using A` is `E7015` unless `A` is `ThreadShared`, whatever its methods do.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Where accepted, identical to B; refuses the fastest shape (a one-thread `Arena`, a bump and no free) for a value whose end touches the arena not at all.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Accepts a race: `struct Pool: slab: Array[u8]; free: Array[usize]` is inferred `ThreadShared` ([THR-9]) and its `deallocate` pushes to `free` on the ending thread while the maker pops it (judgement 1's hole in design 1).
alternatives_weighed.readability: The message blames the arena for a hazard the program has not got.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Contradicts [EXC-15] (a `ref A` can call only methods that read their object) by modelling the word as a `ref A` flatly.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Less safe and slower than B; judged and rejected in the K05 ruling.

alternatives_weighed.name: D: allow only for managers that free nothing one by one (arena only)
alternatives_weighed.what: `thread_shared T using A` accepted only where `A`'s `deallocate` is empty and `T` does not grow; `System`, a `static` manager, a locking pool and a `FoundByAddress` pool refused.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Same as B where accepted; loses `using System` (a block from the platform's allocator, bypassing `Global`'s chunks for large or host-owned memory) and a `ThreadShared` pool whose `deallocate` locks inside.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Same as B (the refused managers are safe under B's property, checked when compiling).
alternatives_weighed.readability: A second exception to learn with no safety behind it.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: A flat list where B states the property that decides every manager alike, a program's own included.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Drops features with no safety gain; a rule that fixes a shape where a property is right (brief rule 7).

alternatives_weighed.name: E: require `FoundByAddress` of every manager a `thread_shared` value uses (never a word)
alternatives_weighed.what: Verdict 47's hope read literally: the instance is always found from the block's address, so no word is ever kept.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Saves nothing: for a `thread_shared` value the word already costs 0 bytes (the queue place); the end pays a mask and a load from the piece's first line (likely cold) instead of one load from the header it already holds. Forces the 65,536-byte piece promise on every pool and every arena.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Same; the promise is the manager writer's `unsafe` one either way.
alternatives_weighed.readability: Every manager author must write the `FoundByAddress` promise to serve shared values.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Verdict 107 names it one of two kinds, not the only kind.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Costs more per end and asks more of every manager than B for a saving B already has by placement.

alternatives_weighed.name: F: a smaller header (16 or 24 bytes) for a value made `using`
alternatives_weighed.what: Drop the home count and the queue place from the header of a value never queued; keep type index, away word and weak count.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Saves 8 to 16 bytes per value (16 MB per million). Costs a layout fork: a class object's address is its header ([OBJ-2], [FFI-35a]), so its fields would lie at a different offset per manager and every method body would be compiled per header size, or the object pointer would have to become the payload address (an ABI change to [OBJ-2], [FFI-35a], the hand-over walk and hot reload); a value that keeps the word needs 8 bytes for it anyway, so the saving is 8 bytes for word-keeping managers and only arena and one-instance managers reach 16.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Unchanged in principle; more header shapes for the runtime routines that see no type to get right.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Departs from verdict 101 ("each object 16 bytes bigger", the measured 32-byte header in every program) and from [OBJ-1]'s one header.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: The bytes saved cost one method body per manager or a new object ABI; refused, and it would depart from verdict 101 for a merely easier memory figure.

alternatives_weighed.name: G: the instance word after the header, the queue place unused (the ruling's doubt 2)
alternatives_weighed.what: Keep verdict 47's word beside the value, 8 bytes beyond the 32-byte header.
alternatives_weighed.speed: 8 bytes more per value for word-keeping managers; and the payload moves by 8, so a class object made in such a manager has its fields at offset 40 against 32 in `Global`: one method body per manager, or an indirection.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Two offsets for one class's fields.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Strictly worse than the queue place, which is free and keeps one object layout.

alternatives_weighed.name: H: a holds-nothing value goes to an unscoped thread from any instance, the instance kept alive by a count
alternatives_weighed.what: A `thread_shared` value made in a local `Arena` may be captured by `thread.spawn`; the arena is kept alive by a run-time count (each value a `thread_shared` owner of its arena) until the last such value ends.
alternatives_weighed.speed: A word per value (the arena owner) and one atomic add at every making and one atomic subtract at every end, on the arena's header, a contended line; a reset of the arena needs a run-time test or a refusal while any value lives, which the compiler could no longer see; verdict 107's measured cost (241 ms and 44.7 MB against 191 ms and 28.2 MB for a million values) returned, and more.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Safe at run time, but a check while running for a property ([LT-4]'s region) the compiler already decides.
alternatives_weighed.readability: The programmer writes nothing and pays always; the alternative lines exist: a scope (`with scope = thread.scope():` from any instance) or a `static` arena.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Contradicts [ALC-5]'s compile-time exclusivity and docs/AUTOPILOT.md §4 (nothing runs unless the property is run-time data).
alternatives_weighed.why_not: The exit check's `static`-instance limit stands; H is refused on speed and on §4.

edits.old: address stands in the header's queue place, and the value costs no word beyond the 32 bytes; so is
edits.new:
address stands in the header's queue place, which only the subtract that takes the away count
  below zero writes (`[RC-4]` point 2), as the away count of a value every owner of which it counts
  never does, so the value costs no word beyond the 32 bytes and its fields lie at the offset they
  have in `Global`, one method body serving every manager (`[OBJ-2]`); so is
edits.why: The owner asked whether the word may sit in the queue place; the rule now says why it may (nothing writes that place for a value counted away from birth) and what the placement buys beyond the 8 bytes (one object layout per class, so no method is compiled per manager), which is the implementation reason shape G was not taken.

edits.old: counted away from the line that makes it and asks no thread which made it (`[RC-4]` point 4).
edits.new:
counted away from the line that makes it and asks no thread which made it (`[RC-4]` point 4). The
  type index of an object made `using A` names the `TypeInfo` of `T using A` (`[RT-3]`), which the
  package that makes one emits as it emits a generic instance (`[MONO-1]`, deduplicated at link),
  whose end function gives the block back as the type says (`[ALC-5a]`: nothing for a manager that
  frees nothing one by one, the instance found from the address for `FoundByAddress`, else a call
  through the kept word), so a runtime routine that sees only the header (`ember_rt_object_release`,
  `[FFI-54]`) ends it as its last owner's end would; one `TypeInfo` per pair of type and manager kind
  a package makes, and nothing while the program runs beyond the end itself.
edits.why: [RC-4] point 4 says the runtime's own routines, which see no type, end such a value, and [ALC-5a] says the give-back is read from the type, never from the block, which carries no mark for it; nothing said how a routine given a bare header learns the manager. A `TypeInfo` per pair is the only shape that keeps both sentences true with no run-time cost and no whole-program fact ([BLD-16]); it holds for every object made `using`, so it is stated where the block's source is.

edits.old: and gives its block back through its manager's `deallocate` on the thread that ends it, nothing for a manager that frees nothing one by one (`[ALC-1]`);
edits.new: and gives its block back through its manager's `deallocate` on the thread that ends it, a direct call (through the word in the header's queue place, one load; a mask and a load for `FoundByAddress`), nothing for a manager that frees nothing one by one (`[ALC-1]`); its handed-over mark is a constant in the header's first store, no instruction beyond the stores every `thread_shared` value's making writes;
edits.why: Every cost has a row: the row priced the count path and the trade but not the making line's mark (nothing: a constant in a store already made) nor how the end finds the instance (one hot load, or a mask and a cold load); an implementer and `ember inspect --cost` read it here.

edits.old: make it in the built-in manager, `st = thread_shared Stats()`, or in a `static` arena"). A value
edits.new:
make it in the built-in manager, `st = thread_shared Stats()`, in a `static` arena, or run the
  thread as a task of a scope that ends before `level`: `with scope = thread.scope():` and
  `scope.spawn(owns fn() owns st: ...)` in place of line 8"). A value
edits.why: The refusal's message named two of the three lines to write; the scope is the one that keeps the arena local and costs nothing, and [TYP-46a] already accepts the value "to a scoped task or a job of a scope from any instance". A refusal is only as friendly as its message (the owner, 2026-10-24).

refused_program:
from std.sync import Atomic
from std.mem import Allocator, Layout
import std.thread

struct Pool:                      # every field is ThreadShared, so Pool is inferred ThreadShared ([THR-9])
    slab: Array[u8]
    free: Array[usize]

# SAFETY: allocate hands out a slot no live value holds; deallocate returns it to `free`
unsafe extend Pool implements Allocator:
    fn allocate(layout: Layout) -> *mut u8:
        i = this.free.pop()                                   # changes `this`
        return this.slab.ptr_at(i * 64)
    unsafe fn deallocate(p: *mut u8, layout: Layout):         # line 12
        this.free.push(owns this.slab.index_of(p))            # changes `this`
    unsafe fn reallocate(p: *mut u8, old: Layout, new_size: usize) -> *mut u8:
        return null                                           # a slot never grows

class Msg:
    hits: Atomic[int] = Atomic(0)

fn main():
    pool = Pool(slab=[], free=[])
    msg = thread_shared Msg() using pool                      # line 23
    with scope = thread.scope():
        scope.spawn(owns fn() owns msg: msg.hits.fetch_add(1))
    println("done")

Refused at line 23 with E7015 ([TYP-46a]): "`msg` would end on whichever thread holds its last owner, and that end gives its block back through `Pool.deallocate` (line 12), which changes `pool`; make it in the built-in manager, `msg = thread_shared Msg()`, or in a manager any thread may call, whose `deallocate` reads `this` and locks inside". The compiler reads this from `Pool`'s own text (or, across a package's edge, from its interface file's summaries, [BLD-14] item 1): `deallocate` changes `this`, so the value would hold the `sharedref mut` link of [LT-4], which is neither `Send` nor `ThreadShared` (verdict 164). With `inner: Mutex[Slab]` and methods that lock inside and read `this`, the same line compiles.
accepted_program:
from std.sync import Atomic
import std.thread

class Stats:
    hits: Atomic[int] = Atomic(0)

fn main():
    level = Arena.with_capacity(64 * 1024)          # frees nothing one by one ([ARN-2]), so the value holds nothing
    stats = thread_shared Stats() using level       # its block is a bump in `level`; every owner is counted in the away count from here
    with scope = thread.scope():
        scope.spawn(owns fn() owns stats: stats.hits.fetch_add(1))   # the task holds the last owner and ends it on its thread
    more = Stats() using level                      # the parent may allocate from `level` meanwhile: the task's end calls nothing on it ([TYP-46a], [THR-11])
    println("done")

Compiles and prints `done`. The making line writes the header once (type index, weak 1, away 1 with the handed-over mark, home 0, queue place 0, since an arena's values keep no word); the spawn is a hand-over the type already decided, so no count moves; the task's end is one acquire-release subtract to zero, the ended compare-exchange, `Stats`'s `drop`, one weak subtract and no call on `level`; `level` ends after the scope, where the compiler saw the last owner end ([ALC-5], [LT-4]). Written `thread_shared Stats() using System`, or `using pool` for a pool whose methods lock inside and read `this`, it compiles the same way; `thread_shared [String("a")] using level` (a value that grows) is E7015, and `thread.spawn(owns fn() owns stats: ...)` in place of the scope is E3063 with the three lines to write.
runtime_cost: For a program that never writes `using` after `thread_shared`: nothing new (0 instructions, 0 bytes; the mark test on the making thread is [RC-4] point 4's existing cost). For a `thread_shared T using A` value: at its making, `A.allocate(Layout(32 + size_of[T], align))` (an arena: a bump and a limit test; `System`: `malloc`), a null test ([ALC-6]), and the same four header stores a `Global` value's making writes, the handed-over mark a constant in the away word's store (0 extra instructions), the instance word stored in the queue place where [ALC-1] keeps one (one store in place of the queue place's null); header 32 bytes, 0 beyond ([OBJ-1]); each +1 one relaxed `fetch_add` and the limit test on its result ([RT-7], [RT-10]), each -1 one acquire-release subtract and a zero test, against the `Global` home path's chunk-header load, thread-local compare, mark load, two branches and a plain add: fewer instructions, more cycles on the making thread (the row's measured 25% on a thread's own values), the same or less on every other thread (no chunk read); at zero the ended compare-exchange, `drop`, one atomic weak subtract, then the give-back as a direct call (`A` known from the type): nothing for a manager that frees nothing one by one, one load of the queue place and the call for a word-keeping manager, a mask and a load for `FoundByAddress`; never the queue push (an atomic exchange), never a check point's work, the end never deferred (lower peak memory for a pipeline). At the boundary: `ember_rt_object_release` and the other routines that see no type load the away word and test the mark (one load and branch, paid for every `thread_shared` value) and end through the `TypeInfo` of `T using A`; one `TypeInfo` per pair of type and manager kind a package makes, at link time. The checks (E7015, E3063, E3021, E7007, E2020) run when compiling and nothing runs for them. §X.4 rows: "A `thread_shared` value's two counts" (edited above) and "A value made `using` a memory manager" (unchanged).
implementer_steps:
1. Types and grammar: `using A` is accepted after `thread_shared T` in a type and after the value on a making line ([GRM-43]: `thread_shared Stats() using level` is `thread_shared (Stats() using level)`); `thread_shared T using A` is a type distinct from `thread_shared T`, a plain `thread_shared T` place being a `using Global` place ([TYP-46]), so `E2020` holds in both directions and every place's type names its values' manager. The package reads only the type written at the line.
2. The property of `A`, at the making line and at a place of the type: from `A`'s declaration in the package, or its interface file across the edge ([BLD-14] item 1 for the summaries of `deallocate` and `reallocate`, item 14 for an empty `deallocate` and `FoundByAddress`): the value holds nothing (empty `deallocate` and `T` does not grow), a `ref A` (`A` is `ThreadShared` and the methods the value's end or growth calls read `this`), or the `sharedref mut` link of [LT-4] (a method called changes `this`); infer `Send` and `ThreadShared` for the value with that link as a component ([TYP-46a], the marker table); refuse with `E7015` at the making line (verdict 165) or at the type where no value could fill it. No whole-program fact is read ([BLD-16]).
3. Regions: the value carries the instance's region as any `using` value ([LT-4], `E3063`; [ALC-5], `E3021`; [ALC-5a] for links); a capture by `thread.spawn`, a job outside a scope or a kept callback is `E3063` unless the instance is a `static` or `static mut`; a scoped task or job takes it from any instance, and [THR-11] counts its growth and end as changes of the instance only where they call its methods.
4. Code for the making line: `p = inst.allocate(Layout(32 + size_of[T], max(align, 8)))`, panic on null ([ALC-6]); one header write: home 0, type index of `T using A` (step 7), weak 1, away = 1 with the handed-over mark, the queue place = the instance address where [ALC-1] keeps a word, else 0; then the constructor or the hand-in of the value.
5. Code for count lines: where the place's type carries `using A` (every typed place, by step 1), emit the away path unconditionally: relaxed `fetch_add` plus limit test, acquire-release subtract plus zero test, the ended compare-exchange at zero ([RT-8], [RT-10]); a `weakref thread_shared T using A` link opens on the away count the same way; never the home path, never a chunk read, never a mark test.
6. The end: `drop`, the atomic weak subtract, and at zero the give-back chosen from the type ([ALC-5a]): no call for an empty `deallocate`, `A.deallocate(block, layout)` through the queue-place word, or through the instance found by [ALC-2]'s mask and load for `FoundByAddress`; the runtime's queue code is untouched, since the away count of such a value never goes below zero.
7. `TypeInfo`: the package that makes a `T using A` value emits a `TypeInfo` for the pair ([RT-3]), named and deduplicated as a generic instance is ([MONO-1], [MNG-1]), whose end function is step 6's; `ember_rt_object_release`, the hand-over walk of [THR-2] and a reload's registration ([HR-12]) test the mark before any chunk read and end through it; [HR-46]'s commit rewrites a `thread_shared` value's instance address in the queue place.
8. Tests: the two programs above; `thread_shared Stats() using System` (compiles, atomic from birth, `free` on any thread); `thread_shared Stats() using Global` equals no `using`; a `ThreadShared` locking pool accepted and the changing pool refused with the message; `thread_shared [0, 0] using level` E7015; the unscoped-thread capture E3063 with the scope line; `into_raw()` of a `using`-made object from a `static` arena released by C with `ember_rt_object_release` (frees nothing, runs `drop`); `ember inspect --cost` reports the row; a stress run ending arena-made values on several threads with the arena reset after the scope.
departs_from_verdict: none. Touched without departure: 19 and 24 (`using` after every owner word, the place names the kind and the line the instance: kept for `thread_shared`); 47 (the pointer is kept where [ALC-1] keeps it and placed in the header's queue place, 0 bytes beyond the header, which is the drop in cost 47 asked the measuring phase for, without dropping the pointer); 101 (the 32-byte header and the two numbers for every value made in `Global` stand; a value made `using` is in fix 2's state from its making line, as N84 and N119 already recorded); 107 (used as written: an empty `deallocate` or `FoundByAddress` gives values with no word, which is what makes a one-thread `Arena` acceptable); 164 (the `sharedref mut` link as the model of a value whose instance's methods change `this`); 165 (refused where the value is made).
prior_art: Rust's `Arc<T, A: Allocator>` (`Arc::new_in`) counts atomically from birth whatever the allocator, stores the allocator in the owner and is `Send` only when `A: Send + Sync`: `Sync` on `A` is exactly Ember's "a manager any thread may call", because Rust's `Allocator::deallocate` takes `&self`, so a pool must lock or use atomics inside to implement it at all; Ember infers the receiver mode from the body ([EXC-15]) instead of declaring it, so the same gate is "`ThreadShared` and the methods read `this`", and a bare `Allocator` bound in a generic body cannot carry it (Rust writes `A: Sync` in the bound; see remaining doubt). C++'s `std::allocate_shared<T>(pmr_alloc, ...)` keeps a copy of the allocator in the control block beside the counts (the analogue of the word in the header) and leaves the allocator's thread safety to the programmer, the race Ember refuses at the line. Objective-C and the JVM keep the object pointer at the header and one header layout per object kind, the reason shape F (a smaller header per manager) forks method bodies. Zig passes `std.mem.Allocator` values explicitly and documents thread safety per allocator, unchecked; Nim's ORC counts non-atomically unless the type is shared. The lesson: allow every allocator, count atomically from birth, gate on the allocator's shareability when compiling, keep one layout; and name the property in a bound for generic code.
odr_ruling_text: Shape B stands as the best of the eight shapes priced for the four goals at once, with four wording and completeness edits and no departure from a verdict. `thread_shared T using A` is allowed for every manager; every owner is counted in the away count from the making line, the path chosen from the type at each line, so a program that never writes the word pays nothing and one that does pays one locked add per count operation in place of the home path's loads and branches (the row's 25% either way, the programmer's choice per value); the mark is a constant in the header's first store; the block is the manager's own work (a bump in an arena, nothing at the end). The instance word sits in the header's queue place, which only the subtract that takes the away count below zero writes, impossible for a value every owner of which that count holds; the placement costs 0 bytes and keeps a class object's fields at one offset whatever manager made it, so one method body serves. A value made `using` loses nothing by never being queued: the queue exists to let the maker read a home count such a value never has, and its end where its last owner ends is what [ALC-5]'s compile-time exclusivity needs. The making line is `E7015` only where the value would hold a link to an instance of a manager that not every thread may call (a `deallocate` or `reallocate` that changes `this`, read from the manager's own text or its interface file), the gate Rust writes as `A: Sync`. The `static`-instance limit on a hand-over to an unscoped thread stands: keeping a local instance alive another way is a run-time count on it for a property the compiler already decides, and a scope from any instance or a `static` instance costs nothing; the `E3063` message now names the scope line too. Added for the implementer: an object made `using A` has the `TypeInfo` of `T using A`, emitted by the package that makes one, so `ember_rt_object_release` and every routine that sees only a header gives the block back as the type says. Not taken: refusing every manager (drops a feature for a hazard the mark removes), the flat `ThreadShared` test (accepts a race), arena-only (drops `System` and locking pools for no safety), `FoundByAddress` for all (one more cold load per end for a saving the queue place already gives), a smaller header per manager (forks every method body or the object ABI, and verdict 101), the word after the header (8 bytes and a second payload offset).
remaining_doubt: (1) A generic body over `[A: needs (Allocator, ThreadShared)]` cannot read from the bound that `A.deallocate` reads `this`, since Ember declares no receiver mode ([EXC-15]: worked out from the body) and `Allocator`'s methods are declared bare ([ALC-2]); under [TYP-17] ("checked once with its parameters standing for any type") a making line `thread_shared T using a` there must be refused (`E7015`, the message naming the bound) until P01 or K34 gives the property a spelling in a bound (Rust's `A: Sync`): either an interface method's first line may say the method only reads its object, promised for every implementation and checked at the `extend`, or a marker for a manager any thread may call, inferred and written only in bounds as `Send` is; outside this ODR, flagged by the K05 ruling's doubt (1) and the critic's item on [ALC-2]. (2) For a `thread_shared` value in a `FoundByAddress` manager the queue place is free, so an implementation could keep the word there and read one hot load at the end instead of a mask and a likely cold load; not proposed, since it adds a third case to [ALC-1]'s two and the saving is one load against the atomic steps already in that end; measurable in the next phase. (3) The trade (a chunk allocation and biased counts against an arena bump and atomic counts) is priced from the brc report and verdict 107's measurements, not measured as one program; the measuring phase should run the accepted program's shape against the same program without `using`. (4) `into_raw()` on a `thread_shared` value ([FFI-54] names `owns T` and a class object with one owner) and the kept-callback token's release are the only routes by which a bare header of a `using`-made value reaches the runtime; the `TypeInfo` edit answers both, and a test should hold it.

item: ODR-260 — A `thread_shared` value made `using` a memory manager
summary: Shape B as Hardened_3 applied it is the best of the shapes weighed: `thread_shared T using A` is allowed, counted in its away count from its making line, refused (`E7015`) only by the property of what the value holds (a link to an instance that not every thread may call), and the instance word, where kept, sits in the header's queue place at 0 bytes. No safe program was found that B accepts and that breaks a promise: the arena case is sound because the value holds nothing and its block lives no longer than the instance's region ([LT-4], [ALC-5], [ALC-5a]'s region mechanism), and the pool case is sound because the end calls only a method that reads `this` on a `ThreadShared` type. The queue place is free by construction (a value whose home count is 0 and whose mark is set in its first store never takes point 2's below-zero subtract), and doubly so by the K10 ruling (a manager that frees one by one and that any thread may call frees under a lock or with atomics, so the value's `drop` carries `Lock` or `Sync`, is not plain, and is marked at its making line by [RC-4] point 4 "by its type" in any case). Four wording defects remain, one of them an implementer-undecidable line: [ALC-5]'s "no change of this rule's kind is made to that instance after the hand-over" for a `static mut` instance is a fact of the program's run that the package compiling the reset's line cannot see ([BLD-16]), so the hand-over to an unscoped thread is limited to a `static` instance, which never changes ([STA-1]) and needs no "after"; [TYP-46a]'s [THR-11] clause leaves open whether an end that calls a reading `deallocate` is a read of the instance (it is, by the method's summary); [RC-4] point 4 gives as its reason a delay that K10's join check point already bounds (the true reason is that the block is not the runtime's); and [ALC-1] states the `using x` name's form where [EXC-15]'s property decides. Shape C (two counts kept, the maker's id in the header's spare bytes, as the biased-counting paper itself lays it out) is sound too and faster for a thread's own values, but it departs from verdict 101 fix 1, needs a fourth header mark for the type-less runtime routines, and loses the free queue place for a word-keeping value whose foreign `deallocate` is plain; it is recorded for the owner, not recommended.

alternatives_weighed.name: A: refuse every manager (E2114 after `thread_shared`)
alternatives_weighed.what: `thread_shared` before a value made `using m` is `E2114`; a shared value's block always comes from the runtime's chunks (the method-3 team's answer; Hardened_2's refusing half).
alternatives_weighed.speed: Every shared value made in bulk pays a runtime chunk allocation and a cross-thread return to the chunk pool, which a bump arena would not; one counting path, but that path already exists for every handed-over value.
alternatives_weighed.readability: `using` follows every owner word but one; the programmer learns an exception that the property does not need.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Drops a feature verdict 19 lists; K34's property ('a type whose value has heap memory of its own takes `using`') gets an exception.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Refuses the gap sweep's program for a hazard counting away from birth removes; the owner's condition on the delegation (never drop a feature to get past a check) weighs against it.

alternatives_weighed.name: B: allowed, counted away from the making line, refused only by what the value holds (applied)
alternatives_weighed.what: `thread_shared T using A` is a `thread_shared T` whose block comes from `A`, marked handed over in its header's first store, every owner counted atomically, the away path emitted from the place's type; `E7015` where the value would hold a link to an instance that not every thread may call; the instance word in the header's queue place.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Nothing new for a program without the word; for one with it, the manager's `allocate` and `deallocate` (a bump and nothing for an arena), atomic count operations from birth, never a check point's work or a chunk-pool return; gives up the home count's plain adds (25% on a thread's own values, [COST-3]).
alternatives_weighed.safety: No accepted program breaks a promise (see refused/accepted programs); the only hazards found were in wording ([ALC-5]'s `static mut` 'after', the [THR-11] clause), fixed below.
alternatives_weighed.readability: One meaning for `using` after every word; the refusal names the manager, the method and the lines to write.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: One code per fact (E2114 a type with no heap memory; E7015 a one-thread thing reaching another thread); one place for the word (verdicts 47 and 107 at 0 bytes); K10's type rule and this rule agree on every word-keeping value.

alternatives_weighed.name: T1: allowed only for a manager any thread may call
alternatives_weighed.what: A flat test on `A` (Hardened_2's E7015 sentence): a one-thread `Arena` is refused even for a value that holds nothing.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Loses the fastest shape (a bump in a one-thread arena, nothing freed, no word).
alternatives_weighed.safety: Safe; refuses for a reason untrue of the arena case ('its end gives its block back to `current`': it does not).
alternatives_weighed.readability: The message blames the arena for a call the value never makes.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Contradicts [TYP-46a]'s own first sentences (a value in a manager that frees nothing one by one holds nothing) and [ARN-2].
alternatives_weighed.why_not: B contains it and decides the arena case by the property instead of the form (brief rule 7).

alternatives_weighed.name: T2: allowed only for managers that free nothing one by one
alternatives_weighed.speed: Same as B for arenas; a locked or atomic pool for shared messages is refused, so those values pay the runtime's chunks.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Drops a feature a program's own `Allocator` could offer safely (a pool that locks inside is ordered by its lock, [STA-1], [THR-13]).
alternatives_weighed.why_not: B contains it; the pool case is sound under the any-thread-may-call property, so refusing it drops a feature to get past a check.

alternatives_weighed.name: T3: no word at all (the instance found from the block's address)
alternatives_weighed.what: Require `FoundByAddress` of every multi-instance manager used with `thread_shared`, so no value keeps a word (verdict 47's hope).
alternatives_weighed.speed: One mask and one load at each end in place of one load; 0 bytes either way, since B's word sits in the free queue place.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Safe, under the `unsafe extend FoundByAddress` promise.
alternatives_weighed.readability: Forces a 64 KiB piece layout on a manager that did not want it.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Verdict 107 made `FoundByAddress` an option, not a requirement.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: B already costs 0 bytes for the word; T3 would drop the plain locked pool for no saving.

alternatives_weighed.name: C: two counts kept, the maker's id in the header's spare bytes
alternatives_weighed.what: A `using`-made value keeps verdict 101's two counts; its making thread is written into the header's unused 4 bytes at the making line and read from there (the biased-counting paper's own layout), the source chosen by the place's type; K10's type and thread rules apply unchanged; the word, where kept, beside the value (8 bytes, verdict 47) or in the queue place only for values K10 marks at birth.
alternatives_weighed.speed: A thread's own `using`-made values 25% faster (the camera program 6x); a pipeline 27% slower on one thread; one 4-byte store at making (the same as B's mark store); the maker's load from the value's own cache line, cheaper than B's chunk-header load for Global values.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Sound under K10: the delayed end is bounded by the join's check point ([RC-4] point 3, 'the one after a `join` or a scope's end makes a value a joined task ended on its own thread end before the parent's next line'), and the instance's reset is E3021 while the task's capture lives; the chain is two rules long where B's is none.
alternatives_weighed.readability: `using` means only where the memory comes from, and every `thread_shared` value counts the same way: the best reading of 'a word on the thing it describes'.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Departs from verdict 101 fix 1 ('The maker's id is read from the object's memory chunk'); needs a fourth header mark ('maker in header') for the runtime routines that see no type, against [OBJ-1]'s 'no flags but a `thread_shared` value's three marks and the kept-by-C mark'; a word-keeping value whose `deallocate` is a plain `@ffi(no_callbacks)` call may be queued, so its word cannot share the queue place and costs 8 bytes; [RC-4] point 4, [OBJ-1], [OBJ-4] and two [COST-3] rows rewritten.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Not the easier shape, but not clearly the better one: it buys speed for one pattern at the price of a second maker source, a new mark and a verdict the owner ruled himself; recorded here so the owner can choose it with its price known (departs from verdict 101: the maker read from the value's header for a block the runtime did not lay out).

alternatives_weighed.name: D: B, with `using System` on a second set of per-thread chunks
alternatives_weighed.what: The runtime lays out `System` blocks in chunks of its own so that a `using System` value keeps the two counts.
alternatives_weighed.speed: Two counts for one rare spelling; a second chunk pool per thread.
alternatives_weighed.readability: `using System` and `using Global` would count differently from every other manager for a reason invisible in the program.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: More runtime machinery for a form few programs write.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Design 1 and the judge rejected it for the same reason; nothing found here changes that.

alternatives_weighed.name: E: the current `static` or `static mut` hand-over limit with the 'after the hand-over' clause
alternatives_weighed.what: The exit check's text: a `using`-made value goes to an unscoped thread from a `static` or `static mut` instance, and no change of [ALC-5]'s kind is made to that instance after the hand-over.
alternatives_weighed.safety: Sound only if every package compiling a `reset()` of a `pub static mut` arena knows whether any function of the program hands a value made in it to an unscoped thread: a fact of the whole program ([BLD-16]), so an implementer cannot decide the reset's line alone.
alternatives_weighed.readability: The message names 'the hand-over's line', which may be in another package.
alternatives_weighed.consistency: Breaks [BLD-16]'s 'No fact of the whole program decides a package's code'.
alternatives_weighed.why_not: Replaced by the `static`-only limit below, which is local: a `static` never changes ([STA-1]), so nothing is checked after the hand-over.

edits.old:
For `[THR-11]` a value's growth and end are
  changes of its instance where they call its methods (a value that holds nothing changes it not at
  all), so two scoped tasks growing values made in one instance are `E7007` naming the instance
edits.new:
For `[THR-11]` a value's growth and end count as the calls they make on its instance, by those
  methods' summaries (`[EFF-24]`): a change of the instance where the method changes it, a read where
  it reads it (a manager any thread may call), and nothing where the value holds nothing; so two
  scoped tasks growing values made in one instance are `E7007` naming the instance
edits.why: The clause said 'changes' flatly and then exempted a manager any thread may call with 'unless', leaving an implementer unable to say whether a task's end that calls a reading `deallocate` is a read of the instance (which conflicts with a parent's or another task's `allocate` that writes a plain field) or nothing. Stating the property, the method's own summary, decides every manager the same way and lets [THR-11]'s existing machinery refuse the mixed pool exactly where its places overlap.

edits.old:
unless `A` is a manager any thread may call, whose `reallocate`
  and `deallocate` read the instance. For the exclusivity rules `[ALC-5]` stands: growth and end are
  the changes of the instance it allows.
edits.new:
and two tasks ending values made in a manager any thread may call read it, which conflicts
  with nothing but a change of what they read (a task making a value in a pool whose `allocate`
  writes a field that its `deallocate` reads, while another task ends a value there, is `E7007`).
  For the exclusivity rules `[ALC-5]` stands: growth and end are the changes of the instance it
  allows.
edits.why: The 'unless' is replaced by what follows from the property: an end that reads the instance is a read for [THR-11], so two ends never conflict and an end conflicts only with a change of the same places.

edits.rule: LT-4 (the hand-over to an unscoped thread)
edits.new:
value made in an instance, a `thread_shared` one included (`[TYP-46a]`), goes to one of them only
  when its instance is a `static`, which lives as long as the program (`[LT-3]`) and never changes
  (`[STA-1]`), so nothing rewinds or frees its memory under the value; from a local, a parameter, a
  field or a `static mut` (which a safe line of the main thread may reset or reassign at any time
  while the thread runs, a fact of the program's run that no package compiling that line can see,
  `[BLD-16]`) it is `E3063` at the hand-over
edits.why: A `static mut` instance lives as long as the program but may be reset; the current text keeps it sound only by [ALC-5]'s 'after the hand-over' clause, a whole-program fact. A `static` never changes, so the hand-over's own line decides, and nothing is checked after it.

edits.old: make it in the built-in manager, `st = thread_shared Stats()`, or in a `static` arena").
edits.new:
make it in the built-in manager, `st = thread_shared Stats()`, or in a `static` manager whose
  `allocate` reads it, a pool that locks inside").
edits.why: A `static` `Arena` cannot be allocated from (`allocate` changes it, `[ALC-1]`), so 'a `static` arena' named a line the language refuses; the message gives the line to write.

edits.old:
one goes to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a
  callback foreign code keeps only from a `static` or `static mut` instance (`[LT-4]`, `E3063`
  otherwise), and from then on lives, for this rule, as long as the instance, so no change of this
  rule's kind is made to that instance after the hand-over (`E3021`, naming the hand-over's line).
edits.new:
one goes to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a
  callback foreign code keeps only from a `static` instance (`[LT-4]`, `E3063` otherwise), which
  never changes (`[STA-1]`), so no change of this rule's kind is ever made to it and nothing is

edits.why: 'after the hand-over' asked the package compiling a `reset()` whether some function of the program had handed a value over before it, a fact of the whole program ([BLD-16]); with the instance a `static`, the rule needs no such fact.

edits.old:
to a scoped task or
  a job of a scope from any instance and to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a callback
  foreign code keeps from a `static` or `static mut` instance alone (`[LT-4]`, `E3063` otherwise)
edits.new:
to a scoped task or
  a job of a scope from any instance and to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a callback
  foreign code keeps from a `static` instance alone (`[LT-4]`, `E3063` otherwise)
edits.why: Follows [LT-4] as corrected; a cross-reference claims what its rule says.

edits.old: a `thread_shared` value made in a local, a parameter or a field instance handed to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a callback foreign code keeps included
edits.new: a `thread_shared` value made in a local, a parameter, a field or a `static mut` instance handed to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a callback foreign code keeps included

edits.old:
and its instance may be reset or end as soon as the
     compiler sees its last owner end (`[ALC-5]`, `[LT-4]`), which an end delayed to a check point
     would miss; so every owner of such a value is counted in its away count, its end is never
     delayed, and the thread that ends it gives the block back through the manager's `deallocate`
     there.
edits.new:
and the runtime's chunk pools never hold it, so there is no
     thread to queue it to and no pool to return it to; so every owner of such a value is counted in
     its away count, its end never waits for a check point, its instance is free as soon as the
     compiler sees its last owner end (`[ALC-5]`, `[LT-4]`), and the thread that ends it gives the
     block back through the manager's `deallocate` there.
edits.why: The reason given, that a delayed end would miss the instance's reset, is contradicted by point 3 as K10 wrote it ('the one after a `join` or a scope's end makes a value a joined task ended on its own thread end before the parent's next line'), and a local instance is reached by another thread only through a scoped task or job, which a join bounds. The rule now gives the reason that holds, the block is not the runtime's, and states the immediate end as the consequence it is.

edits.rule: §X.4 [COST-3] row "A value made `using` a memory manager"
edits.old: a value whose manager may have several instances keeps one word, its instance's address, so that its growth and its end go back to that instance;
edits.new: a value whose manager may have several instances keeps one word, its instance's address, so that its growth and its end go back to that instance (a `thread_shared` value in its header's queue place, `[OBJ-1]`, so no byte beyond the header);
edits.why: Every cost has a row: the row priced the word at one word for every value, and [OBJ-1] places a `thread_shared` value's word in the header, at no byte beyond the 32.

edits.new:
`using x` names the instance
  through a name that may change it (its owner, a `ref mut` name, or a `sharedref mut` link) where
  its `allocate` changes the instance (`[EXC-15]`, `[ALC-5]`), and through any name where its
  `allocate` reads it (a manager any thread may call that locks inside, `[TYP-46a]`, and a `static`,
  `[STA-1]`);
edits.why: The sentence fixed the name's form; [EXC-15] decides by the method's body, and the rule's own later sentence ('a manager with one instance is a `static` whose `allocate` reads `this`') and [TYP-46a]'s pool that locks inside already need the reading case. The E3023 sentence that follows stays, since its `allocate` changes the arena.

refused_program:
from std.arena import Arena
from std.sync import Atomic
import std.thread

static mut FRAME: Arena = Arena(1 << 20)          # the main thread's arena; any function of the main thread may write `FRAME.reset()`

class Stats:
    hits: Atomic[int] = Atomic(0)

fn start() -> JoinHandle[void]:
    st = thread_shared Stats() using FRAME         # line 10: holds nothing ([TYP-46a]), so far accepted
    return thread.spawn(owns fn() owns st: st.hits.fetch_add(1))     # line 11: to an unscoped thread

fn tick():
    FRAME.reset()                                  # line 14: rewinds the arena under `st` whenever `start` ran first

fn main():
    h = start()
    tick()
    h.join()

Under the current text line 11 is accepted (`[LT-4]`: "only when its instance is a `static` or `static mut`") and line 14 is `E3021` only "after the hand-over" (`[ALC-5]`), which the package compiling `tick` cannot know: whether `start` runs before `tick` is a fact of the program's run, and with `pub static mut FRAME` the hand-over may be in another package ([BLD-16]). Under the edits line 11 is refused when compiling: E3063 ([LT-4]) "`st` was made in `FRAME` (line 10), a `static mut` that a safe line of the main thread may reset while the thread started on line 11 still holds `st`; make it in the built-in manager, `st = thread_shared Stats()`, or in a `static` manager whose `allocate` reads it, a pool that locks inside". Nothing runs for the check. The pool case stays as the text has it: `msg = thread_shared Msg() using pool` for a `Pool` whose `deallocate` pushes to a plain `free` list is E7015 at that line ([TYP-46a]), "`msg` would end on whichever thread holds its last owner, and that end gives its block back through `Pool.deallocate` (line 12), which changes `pool`; make it in the built-in manager, `msg = thread_shared Msg()`, or in a manager any thread may call, whose `deallocate` reads `this` and locks inside".
accepted_program:
from std.arena import Arena
from std.sync import Atomic
from std import mem
import std.thread

class Stats:
    hits: Atomic[int] = Atomic(0)

fn main():
    level = Arena(1 << 20)                        # frees nothing one by one ([ARN-2]), so a value made in it holds no link to it
    stats = thread_shared Stats() using level     # a bump in `level`; its header's first store sets the handed-over mark; every owner is counted atomically from here, chosen from this type
    with scope = thread.scope():
        worker = thread_shared stats              # one more owner: one atomic add and its limit test, no test of the mark
        scope.spawn(owns fn() owns worker: worker.hits.fetch_add(1))   # the task ends `worker` on its own thread: one atomic subtract, and no call on `level`
        stats.hits.fetch_add(1)                   # the parent reads the same object meanwhile: `Stats` is `ThreadShared`
    println(stats.hits.load())                    # 2; the scope's end joined the task
    mem.drop(owns stats)                          # the last owner: the end's compare-exchange, `drop`, the weak count's subtract, and nothing given back
    level.reset()                                 # allowed: no value made in `level` lives ([ALC-5]); above the drop it would be E3021

Compiles and prints 2. The value is `Send` and `ThreadShared` because it holds nothing ([TYP-46a]), so it goes to the scoped task; it could not go to a `thread.spawn` thread from `level`, a local (E3063, [LT-4]). The same program with `stats = thread_shared Stats()` keeps the two counts and a block from the runtime's chunks; the programmer chooses by the word, and the [COST-3] row prices the trade. A `static POOL: LockedPool` whose `allocate` and `deallocate` lock inside and read `this` (a manager any thread may call) gives `msg = thread_shared Msg() using POOL` that may go to a `thread.spawn` thread as well: its end on that thread calls `POOL.deallocate` under the pool's lock, through the instance word in the header's queue place, and `POOL` never changes ([STA-1]).
runtime_cost: For a program that writes no `using` after `thread_shared`: nothing new; the edits are all decided when compiling (E3063, E7007, E7015) and two are wording of cost rows. For a `thread_shared T using A` value: at its making, one call of `A.allocate` (a bump for an arena, a lock for a pool that locks inside) and the header's stores (type index, weak 1, home 0, away = 1 with the handed-over mark, the instance word in the queue place where [ALC-1] keeps one); every owner made is one relaxed atomic add with the limit test on the returned value, every owner ended one acquire-release atomic subtract, the end one compare-exchange on the away word ([RC-4] points 1 and 2, [RT-8], [RT-10]), all emitted from the place's type with no load-and-branch on the mark; never a check point's work, never the queue, never a cross-thread return to a chunk pool; at the end `drop`, the weak count's subtract and `A.deallocate` through the word, by address for `FoundByAddress`, or no call for a manager that frees nothing one by one (verdict 107). Against a value made in `Global` it gives up the home count's plain adds (a thread's own values 25% faster, the camera program 89 ms against 544 ms, the brc report) for the manager's allocation and no runtime free (a pipeline, made on one thread and ended on another, is 27% faster on one thread with the atomic path). §X.4 rows: "A `thread_shared` value's two counts" (already prices the away path, the mark test's absence and the trade) and "A value made `using` a memory manager" (edited: the word costs no byte beyond the header for a `thread_shared` value). The runtime's type-less routines (`ember_rt_object_release`, the hand-over walk, a reload's registration) pay the one load and one branch on the mark they already pay, now ordered before any chunk read.
implementer_steps: 1. Types: `using A` is accepted after a `thread_shared T` type and after a `thread_shared X(...)` value on a making line ([GRM-43] binds the word on the value, [TYP-46]); `thread_shared T using A` is a type distinct from `thread_shared T`, a plain place being a `using Global` place (E2020 both ways, [TYP-46]), so every place's type names its values' manager ([BLD-16]). 2. For every type implementing `Allocator`, from the declaration the compiling package sees (its source or its interface file, [BLD-14] items 1 and 14): whether `deallocate` is empty, whether it implements `FoundByAddress`, whether the type is `ThreadShared`, and the receiver summary of `allocate`, `deallocate` and `reallocate` ([EXC-15], [EFF-24]); "any thread may call" = `ThreadShared` and `deallocate` and `reallocate` read `this`. 3. At `thread_shared X(...) using a` and at a type `thread_shared T using A`: decide what the value holds ([ALC-1], [TYP-46a]): nothing (empty `deallocate` and `T` does not grow), a `ref A` (keeps the word or `FoundByAddress`, `A` any thread may call), else a `sharedref mut` link; infer `Send`/`ThreadShared` for the value with that link; E7015 with [TYP-46a]'s message where it is not; verdict 165's `ThreadShared(T)` check beside it. In a generic body the check runs per instance, whose body the instantiating package compiles ([BLD-16] last sentence, [TYP-16]), the message naming the chain ([DIA-27]). 4. Regions: the value carries the instance's region ([LT-4]); a hand-over to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a kept callback is allowed only where the instance is a `static` (E3063 otherwise, by the instance's declaration, local to the line); a scoped task's or job's owned capture lives until its join for [ALC-5]'s liveness, as a link does for [ALC-5a]. 5. [THR-11]: a `using` value's growth and end contribute the summaries of the `Allocator` methods they call to the task's claims (a change, a read, or nothing); conflicts are decided by the existing place-level check. 6. Code for the making line: `p = a.allocate(Layout(32 + size_of[T], max(align, 8)))`, panic on null ([ALC-6]); header stores: home 0, type index, weak 1, away = 1 with the handed-over mark set, the instance address in the queue place where the value keeps one; publish with a release ([RT-8]). 7. Count lines where the place's type carries `using A` (A not `Global`): emit the away fast paths unconditionally ([RT-10]); where it is plain `thread_shared T`: today's code (the mark decides). `weakref thread_shared T using A` links open on the away count from the type ([RC-5] point 2). 8. Drop glue per type: the end's compare-exchange, `drop`, the atomic weak subtract, then `deallocate` through the queue-place word, by [ALC-2]'s mask and load, or no call; the queue code is untouched. 9. Runtime: `ember_rt_object_release`, the [THR-2] hand-over walk and [HR-12]'s registration test the handed-over mark before computing any chunk address; [HR-46]'s rewrite of instance addresses reads a `thread_shared` value's word from the queue place (an implementer note). 10. Tests: the two programs above; the pool with a plain `free` list refused and the same pool under a `Mutex` accepted; `thread_shared Stats() using System` atomic from birth; `using Global` equal to no `using`; the `static mut` arena hand-over E3063 and the `static` locked pool to a spawned thread accepted; break tests: drop the mark from the first store and release from a C thread (reads arena bytes as a chunk header); remove the mark-before-chunk order in `ember_rt_object_release`.
prior_art: Rust: `Arc::new_in(A: Allocator)` stores the allocator inline in the control block (`&A` is 8 bytes, `Global` 0) and counts atomically for every `Arc`, so B's atomic-from-birth path costs what every Rust `Arc` costs; `Arc<T, A>: Send` requires `A: Send` and `Sync` requires `A: Sync`, and since `Allocator::deallocate` takes `&self` a thread-safe allocator must synchronise inside, which is exactly Ember's "any thread may call" (a `ThreadShared` type whose `deallocate` reads `this`); a `bumpalo::Bump` is `!Sync`, so Rust refuses the arena case outright (shape T1), while verdict 107's compile-time fact "its `deallocate` does nothing" lets Ember accept it by the property of what the value holds. C++: `std::allocate_shared` over a `pmr::polymorphic_allocator` keeps a pointer to the `memory_resource` in the control block (8 bytes) and counts atomically; thread safety of the resource is unchecked (`monotonic_buffer_resource` is documented not thread-safe, and the program may race), which is the race Ember refuses with E7015. Zig: an `std.mem.Allocator` is a two-word vtable passed explicitly and stored where the value needs it; thread safety is the allocator's documentation (`ThreadSafeAllocator` wraps a lock). Swift and Nim have no per-value allocator for class instances. Choi, Shull and Torrellas, "Biased Reference Counting" (2018), the source of verdict 101, keep the owner thread's id in the object's own header word; verdict 101's fix 1 moved it to the memory chunk, which is why a block the runtime did not lay out has no maker and why shape C (the paper's layout for `using`-made values) is the natural alternative if the owner wants the two counts there. Lesson: every mature design makes "which thread may free" a property of the allocator type, checked (Rust) or documented (C++, Zig); Ember's B checks it from the method's summary and goes one step further by accepting the arena case the trait systems cannot express.
odr_ruling_text: **Ruling.** Shape B stands as the best of the shapes weighed, with wording fixes: `thread_shared T using A` is allowed, every owner is counted in its away count from the making line (the path emitted from the place's type, no test of the mark), the instance word, where [ALC-1] keeps one, stands in the header's queue place at no byte beyond the 32 (a value marked at its first store never takes point 2's below-zero subtract, and by K10 a word-keeping value's `drop` carries `Lock` or `Sync` and is marked at birth in any case), and the making line is `E7015` only where the value would hold a link to an instance that not every thread may call; a value that holds nothing (an `Arena`, [ARN-2]) is accepted, and a pool whose `deallocate` writes a plain field is refused with the line to write. Shape A drops a feature for a hazard that counting away from birth removes; shape C (the two counts kept, the maker's id in the header's spare bytes, as the biased-counting paper lays it out) is sound under K10's join check point and 25% faster for a thread's own values, but departs from verdict 101 fix 1, needs a fourth header mark and loses the free queue place; it is recorded for the owner, not taken. Four corrections of the text: the hand-over to an unscoped thread, a job outside a scope or a kept callback is allowed from a `static` instance alone, since a `static mut` may be reset by a safe line and [ALC-5]'s "after the hand-over" was a fact of the whole program ([BLD-16]); [TYP-46a]'s [THR-11] clause states that growth and end count as the calls they make (a change, a read, or nothing); [RC-4] point 4 gives the reason that holds (the block is not the runtime's, so there is no thread to queue it to) in place of a delay K10's join check point already bounds; [ALC-1] lets `using x` name a manager whose `allocate` reads it through any name. What a `using`-made value loses by never being queued is the home count's plain adds on its making thread (25% on a thread's own values); what it gains is a bump allocation, no runtime free, an end that never waits, and the free slot for its word. For the owner: whether B's trade, chosen per value by the word, is what he wants, or shape C's uniform two counts at its price.
remaining_doubt: (1) Generic bodies: `[A: needs (Allocator, ThreadShared)]` cannot say that `A.deallocate` reads `this`; [BLD-16]'s last sentence ("What a generic function changes through its type parameters' methods is worked out for each instance, whose body the instantiating package compiles") and [TYP-16] make the E7015 a per-instance refusal naming the chain, which is sound but late; a marker for "a manager any thread may call" would be a new word, so it is left to K34/P01 with [ALC-2]'s missing receiver modes. (2) B's soundness in the arena case rests on a scoped task's owned capture living, for [ALC-5]'s E3021, until its join; [ALC-5a] uses exactly this region mechanism for links and [THR-11] checks a task's claims until the join, but no sentence says it of an owned capture in so many words (a gap of P02, noted by design 2 too). (3) The `static`-only limit removes `static mut FRAME: Arena` as a source of values for unscoped threads; no std arena has an `allocate` that reads `this`, so arena-made values reach unscoped threads only through a program's own locking manager until std offers one (`ThreadArena` is the job-local arena of [JOB-5], `ref mut`, not that). (4) The trade in the [COST-3] row is priced from the brc report and verdict 107's measurements, not measured as one program; shape C's numbers would need the measuring phase. (5) [HR-46]'s rewrite of a `thread_shared` value's instance address from the queue place is an implementer note the text does not spell; [HR-46] already requires the runtime to enumerate every such address.
